Proposition
[$Q$ is a heat subsolution] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0132, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0133, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0134, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0135, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0136, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0137, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0138 ↗ lem:chow-iv-symmetrized-third-derivative-evolution 1. ch29:29.44\group The $Q$ Invariant

The quantity $Q=v|\operatorname {TF}(B)|^2$ satisfies \[ (\partial _t-v\Delta _{S^2})Q\le 0. \] Equivalently, because $\Delta _g=v\Delta _{S^2}$, it is a subsolution of the heat equation of $g(t)$.
